newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end down on poor market prospects.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end down on poor market prospects.

text.p: Seoul stocks finished weaker on Wednesday as bearish market prospects, prompted by shrinking customer deposits, kept investors away, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed down 8.71 points to 744.99. Losers outpaced gainers 428 to 373. Volume remained thin at 37.28 million.
Large-cap counters took a beating whereas selected small-sized stocks gained on speculative buying, brokers said.
The securities sector led the fall, with the securities sub-index down 5.94 percent to 1,264.36 points.
Brokerage houses are expected to be hit by competition after they are given the right to set their own commission fees from September, brokers said.
Profit-takers also hammered the securities shares after gains in late May and early June, they said.
Ssangyong Securities dropped to its daily limit low of 8,280 won, down 720.
Brokers said margin loans at brokerage houses have recently moved ahead of customer deposits, dampening the sentiment.
Margin loans had steadily risen to 3.32 trillion won as of Monday, while customer deposits, which had been narrowing for the past week, were tallied at 3.31 trillion.
"Consolidation is likely to continue on deterioration of the supply and demand situation," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
Kia Group shares were mixed on news that Korea Development Bank had decided to extend 30 billion won in emergency loans to the debt-stricken Kia Steel a unit of the Kia Group.
Kia Steel fell 50 won to 3,200, while Kia Motors rose 200 won to 13,600.
Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store closed limit up on news that its parent Dainong Group had agreed to cede management rights of both firms to creditors, brokers said.
Dainong shares surged to 3,440 won, up 250 won, while Midopa stocks rose to 8,200 won, up 600.
Samsung Electronics shares closed unscathed despite a lawsuit by a shareholder seeking to nullify privately-placed convertible bonds, accusing Samsung of hurting small investors.
